_expect.name: Bald Knob Cliff AKA: Lost World Crag

nh_4_bald_knob_cliff_aka_lost_world_crag.blurb: A small cliff at the far right end of the Slablands in the Yellowjacket crags near Waterville Valley, sitting in the col at the south end of the Acteon Range. It holds eleven routes, mostly trad with a handful of bolted lines, and the grades run widely from easy fifth class through the low and mid 5.10s and 5.11s up to a few in the 5.12 and 5.13 range. The terrain mixes friction slab, a prominent crack and a steep blank wall, so expect a mix of gear and bolt-protected climbing. It is a quiet spot with room for more development, and the best-known line is a two-pitch crack-and-slab outing.

nh_2_the_cakewalk_area.blurb: A broad, open face at Humphrey's Ledge near North Conway, enclosed by a buttress on each side with a steep wall or roof above. Eleven trad routes cover the middle grades, mostly 5.7 to 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.9 and low 5.10 range, and most run one to three pitches. The face collects plenty of sun and dries quickly, so it suits cold days in late fall, winter and early spring. Despite the ledge's reputation for loose rock, this wall is described as clean and well protected, and several older bold lines have been cleaned and bolted. It is probably the most visited section of Humphrey's.

nh_2_south_face.blurb: The first group of ice flows you meet at Frankenstein Cliff in Crawford Notch, seen from the road high above the railway line just short of the Amphitheater. Eleven routes: ten water-ice lines and one mixed route, with most sitting at WI4 and a couple at the easier and harder ends of the range. This is the more serious end of the cliff, and the ice forms over granite, so the mixed lines are technical. Formation depends heavily on the weather, and falling ice is a real concern on sunny days. Newer hard mixed lines are still being added at the south end.

nh_west_end_the.blurb: The western section of Owl's Head Cliff in Oliverian Notch, covering everything left of the big wet black gully. Eleven routes, nine of them trad and two sport, spanning roughly 5.6 to the low 5.12s with a good chunk at 5.11. The rock is steep granite slab. Most lines are long multi-pitch adventures; the only modern, bolted climbs are on the wall just beside the gully, while the rest are committing slabs with aging hardware. Reach the base by following the trail left and downhill from the Nose. Not a place for a quick casual day.
